clue.text: Get shot of one odd clue to mock

parts.note: to get shot of something is British slang for getting rid of it
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, telling us to rearrange the letters of clue

explanation.surface: Someone discards a strange crossword clue so as to make fun of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule as a verb is a direct synonym of mock, both meaning to deride or make fun of.

clue.text: Beast providing your opening to approve

parts.note: a rat is an animal, here a beast
providing in the sense of on condition that means if

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from your

explanation.surface: A creature supplies your start so that something can be approved.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty or decision is formally to approve or confirm it.

clue.text: Beast and men beheaded and died to be put in tray

parts.note: a dog is an animal, a beast

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, of men is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before its head goes
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A grim scene of slaughtered animals and men, their bodies laid in a tray.
explanation.walkthrough: The tray is an ashtray: a dog-end is the British slang name for a cigarette stub, the thing one stubs out there.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette butt is something you drop into an ashtray, so it is described by what is done with it.

clue.text: Beast let out beasts

parts.note: a cat is an animal, a beast

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered tells us to rearrange the letters of let

explanation.surface: An animal releases a herd of other animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are farm animals, cows and oxen, collectively beasts in old farming usage.

clue.text: Assistant place holder?

parts.note: lieu is French-derived for place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant holds a property, so is a holder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an assistant is just a person keeping a seat warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself means one holding the place of another, which is why a lieutenant is a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a deputy or second in command who assists a superior.

clue.text: Far off help, I'm sorry to say

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong signals rearranging the letters of far

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Help is a long way off, someone apologises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' is part of the surface: the definition works in the phrase 'I'm afraid', meaning I'm sorry to say.
explanation.definitionFit: In polite apology, being afraid that something is so means being sorry to have to say it.

clue.text: Beast with cover for plant

parts.note: a fox is a wild animal, a beast
a glove is a covering for the hand

explanation.surface: An animal is supplied with protective covering in place of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove, digitalis, is a tall flowering garden and woodland plant.

clue.text: Debate causing a schism about sticky stuff

indicators.note: about means around, so the split goes round the sticky stuff

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split, a schism
gum is an adhesive, sticky stuff

explanation.surface: A row arises from a split over some sticky business.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a reasoned debate as well as a quarrel.

clue.text: Ballet girl uses variety in Hamlet

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for Hamlet

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so a Dane

indicators.note: a variety is a new mix, so the letters of uses are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballerina finds various uses for herself in a production of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, the feminine of danseur.

clue.text: In unison to acquire woman

parts.note: to get something is to acquire it
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A suitor, harmonising, sets out to win a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things together means doing them jointly, all at once, in unison.

clue.text: Beast with craving to accept good publicity, perhaps

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the craving holds the letter for good

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: A hungry animal seems ready to take some favourable press.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Margaret Thatcher's phrase 'the oxygen of publicity': publicity is something that keeps a cause alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity is figuratively the oxygen that keeps a cause alive, so it is a metaphorical example.

clue.text: Conclusive nature of one faintly discernable

indicators.note: the letters of one and faintly can be discerned, made out, in a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A conclusion is only faintly visible to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discernable' signals rearranging I (one) and FAINTLY together; the clue's words promise faint visibility, not a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Finality is the quality of being final, so the conclusive nature of a decision.

clue.text: Beast in iron — and in spirit on fire

indicators.note: in puts the animal inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a lamb is a young sheep, a beast

explanation.surface: An animal cooked in an iron pan, with flaming spirits poured over.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambé dish is served with brandy or other spirits poured over and set alight.

clue.text: Beast between poles on organ on the eastern seaboard

indicators.note: between puts the animal inside the two poles

parts.note: N for north pole, taken twice here as two poles
a ewe is a female sheep
a gland is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: An animal stands between two poles over some organ on the Atlantic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on organ' is a down clue's way of putting GLAND under the rest. Both poles here are N. The region is the north-eastern corner of the US Atlantic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The New England states lie along the north-eastern Atlantic seaboard of the United States.

clue.text: Gets in the way, which 10 is never going to

definitions.meaning: to intervene is to step in or interfere
read as ..., between veins, where oxygen (the answer to 10) does not go

explanation.surface: Something keeps obstructing, unlike a gas that never interferes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into Latin inter (between) and venes (veins): oxygen travels within the vessels, never between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene means to come between, so obstruct or get in the way of something.

clue.text: Beast among half of at least 24 people in charge of a remote age

indicators.note: among places the beast in the middle of the other pieces
half of means only the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: a jury has twelve members, so juries in the plural have at least 24 people
an ass is a donkey, a beast

explanation.surface: A donkey stands among a crowd of jurors who govern some distant era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jurassic is a geological period around 150 million years ago, an extremely remote age.

clue.text: Beast of legend, not so important round the cross

indicators.note: round means the less important word goes round the cross

parts.note: minor means lesser or less important
the tau cross is a T-shaped cross named after the Greek letter

explanation.surface: A lesser figure circles a cross, a creature from myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur is the half-bull monster of Greek legend kept in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Recipe advice from saint on Manchester stream

parts.note: the Irwell is the river flowing through Manchester and Salford

explanation.surface: A holy figure on the banks of a Manchester river offers cooking tips.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irwell is the river dividing Manchester from Salford in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir well is a familiar instruction in recipes, telling the cook to mix thoroughly.

clue.text: Loveless marriage nursed by mistake

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so the O is taken out

parts.note: a union is a marriage
to tend a patient is to nurse them

explanation.surface: A loveless marriage was kept going by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means O, nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unintended was not meant, so it happened accidentally, by mistake.

clue.text: Overenthusiastic use of weapon on half the spirits

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: half the means only the first three of the six letters survive

parts.note: ghosts are spirits

explanation.surface: Firing a gun at half the spectres seems rather overzealous.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho describes someone eager to the point of recklessness, over-keen.

clue.text: Did wrong in performance but I can't give it up

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for performance

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of did are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer erred in a show yet cannot quit the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns DID into DDI, which goes 'in' the act.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is someone dependent on a habit, who would say they cannot abandon it.

clue.text: Beast with soldier and organ

parts.note: a kid is a young goat
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals, a famous soldier

explanation.surface: An animal, a soldier and an organ are listed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidney is one of the paired organs that filter the blood.

clue.text: Beast in poster on ship

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the advert

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, an ad
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A creature pictured on a poster aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a ship, aircraft or train.

clue.text: Beast in turning aside part of the Mass

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the rearranged word
turning means changing round, so the letters of aside are rearranged

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

explanation.surface: An animal turns aside during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes ASDEI from ASIDE, and the gnu goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Lamb of God, is a prayer sung or said in the Mass.

clue.text: Beast in ship with investments

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the abbreviation for ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a hare is a long-eared animal

explanation.surface: An animal travels aboard a ship along with financial holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares are units of ownership in a company bought as investments.

clue.text: Beast follows mob that's swelling

indicators.note: follows means the beast comes after the mob

parts.note: a gang is a mob
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A big cat trails a gang of people who have some lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cyst or swelling, typically on a tendon at the wrist.

clue.text: Beast led astray to cause milk problem

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering dog is led off and spoils the milk.
explanation.definitionFit: When milk curdles it separates into lumps, so causing it to go off is to curdle it.

clue.text: Idolatry organised with skill

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of idolatry are rearranged

explanation.surface: Idol worship has been skilfully arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something adroitly is to do it deftly, cleverly and skilfully.
